neighbours.label: the change noun after a percentage or amount ('a 15 percent rise', 'a 10% decrease', 'a 6-point drop'): the size of a change being named
fire: Ticket sales hit 2 million, a 30 percent increase from the year before.
Exports fell sharply last quarter, an 8% decline from the spring.
The city recorded 410 burglaries, a 12 percent drop over 2021.
Rents climbed again in March, a 5 percent rise in a single month.
Hospital visits reached 9,000, a 20% jump compared with last winter.
The firm's profit was $4 million, a 40 percent fall from 2019.
Turnout was 61 percent, a three-point increase on the previous vote.
Coffee prices reached a record high, a 25% surge since January.
quiet: Ticket sales hit 2 million, and 30 percent of buyers were students.
Exports fell sharply last quarter as ports closed for repairs.
The city recorded 410 burglaries, mostly in the northern districts.
Rents climbed again in March as more families moved to the area.
Hospital visits reached 9,000, with 20% of patients over seventy.
The firm's profit was $4 million, most of it from overseas sales.
Turnout was 61 percent, with long queues at many polling stations.
Coffee prices reached a record high after frost hit the farms.

predictions: fire 0.4-0.7 on rise/increase/decrease/drop after a number; a percentage of a whole ('15 percent of students') and change words without a number below 0.1
notes: Probe: '15 percent rise' 0.578, '10% decrease' 0.461, '$300 less' 0.117, '12 per cent' 0.067; '15 percent of the students' 0.033, 'strong growth' 0.025. The change noun after a quantity carries it.
